title: TESS centroids show that 13% of main-sequence M-dwarf rapid rotators have another star's period; after cleaning, contraction alone predicts 3.5 main-sequence CPVs for 2 seen
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. Earlier campaign results found that old main-sequence M dwarfs at the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x of young CPV hosts have 2 CPVs where a contraction-only (x-only) model predicts 8.9, and that eROSITA X-ray weights reduce the prediction to 4.4. We located the source of the rotation signal for all 4,595 TESS 2-minute rapid rotators of these tests (P 0.08-2 d, BP-RP 2.4-3.8), with flux-weighted centroids of 7,972 light curves. The signal is more than 7 arcsec from the target for 13.3% (11.5-15.2%) of main-sequence rapid rotators, against 5.4% of 1-24 Myr members and 2.5% of 35-750 Myr members, and for 46% of main-sequence stars with P < 0.2 d. At fixed crowding, magnitude, period and neighbour flag, the main-sequence odds are 4.4 times higher (p = 3e-15). Off-target main-sequence stars are mostly X-ray quiet (58%, against 6% of on-target stars), so the two independent methods agree. With off-target stars removed and X-ray weights, the x-only model predicts 3.5 (95% interval 1.7-5.6) main-sequence CPVs for 2 observed (p = 0.37); the extra main-sequence rate factor at fixed x is 0.55 (0.09-1.82). Threshold variants give 3.4-4.0 (p = 0.29-0.43). The age decline inside young groups does not change (e-folding 41 Myr at fixed P; radius exponent gamma 0.65, 0.35-1.40). Thus no age factor beyond contraction is necessary, but a factor down to about 0.1 is still allowed. Limitations: 2 main-sequence CPVs; the centroid method cannot separate sources within about 5 arcsec; X-ray data cover half the sky; neighbour-clean main-sequence stars still have 0 CPVs for 2.2 predicted (p = 0.16).

citations.reason: We repeat its frozen x-only main-sequence CPV test. Off-target TESS periods inflated its prediction; with centroid and X-ray cleaning the deficit (8.9 predicted, 2 observed) becomes 3.5 predicted (p = 0.37). We reuse its S1-S55 periods, labels, efficiencies and features.

We do the TESS centroid check that it named as open. X-ray-quiet main-sequence stars are mostly off target, which supports its inference; combined with its X-ray weights the remaining deficit disappears. We reuse its code.
Its contraction (x-only) model agrees with the cleaned main-sequence count; its gamma result does not change after cleaning.
